@mm4tt @wojtek-t found a case that external IP may be actually required. The test `should work for type=NodePort` checks the client ip, if we access the service from a test container, we would only get the ip address of the test container rather then the client https://github.com/knight42/kubernetes/blob/001e9fd5bc38ab2e444725e47aa892884efe1467/test/e2e/network/service.go#L3151-L3157

> Matt Matejczyk Wojciech Tyczynski found a case that external IP may be actually required. The test `should work for type=NodePort` checks the client ip, if we access the service from a test container, we would only get the ip address of the test container rather then the client https://github.com/knight42/kubernetes/blob/001e9fd5bc38ab2e444725e47aa892884efe1467/test/e2e/network/service.go#L3151-L3157

Actually, the test pod ip will be the client ip in that case. We should just check that the client ip we got matches the ip of the `TestContainerPod`- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/708fb6b457d94c770890731e53090a975f53679a/test/e2e/framework/network/utils.go#L123. So the check should be something like:
```
if clientIp != config.TestContainerPod.Status.PodIP {
  framework.Failf("Source IP was NOT preserved")
}
```

The reason for this failure is exactly https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/90047

What is happening in this test is:
- GetEndpointNodes is faulty: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/network/service.go#L2928
- it first get up to 3 schedulable nodes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/126bb79201227164caf799798c89da44301d0e27/test/e2e/framework/service/jig.go#L263
- then it joins it with nodes where are endpoints (in this test 1)
- so in 5k cluster we very rarely get match and return empty list
- however, if we have a match, we're running private nodes (without public IPs) and then it explodes

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92163 should address this issue

Let me get back to that PR.

review_comments: Let's move this function to jig.go (make it method of jig the same way as GetEndpointNodes is.

Currently we already have a similar method, i.e. `jig.GetEndpointNodesWithIP(corev1.NodeInernalIP)`，it returns a map of node names -> list of internal IPs and would return empty list if no IP found.

I put the function `getEndpointNodesWithInternalIP` here because I think this function would only be used here, and it returns a map of node names -> ip(rather than a list of IP) and it would return an error if no IP found.
Given that we have a presubmit now, let's remove the `DisabledForLargeClusters` tag from this particular test to make sure our fix works.

000 ?

Then this method would return 0, which is not what we want, right?

it is kind of difficult to tell the errors caused by curl(such as fail to connect to remote, resolve host, etc.) from the errors caused by executing command in the test container(such as fail to connect to the api server). IMHO the former errors are retriable while the latter are not(I suppose it indicates that the cluster might be misconfigured), I think returning 0 is sufficient to let users know curl is sucessfully executed but it cannot connect to the host.

I am not sure if there is a better choice, any suggestion is welcome.
